subject: BrightLeaf price simulation & target benchmarking
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <emorales@brightleaf.ai>, procurement@brightleaf.ai
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Sep 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: BrightLeaf price simulation & target benchmarking

Hi Elena — thanks again for a productive call earlier. Quick recap and the asks we agreed on so we’re aligned:

Summary of BrightLeaf needs (as I understood them)
- Primary usage: document summarization pipeline (batch + async) — peak ~300M tokens/month, baseline ~220M tokens/month.
- Secondary usage: conversational triage (chat assist) — 40–60M tokens/month, spikes during business hours.
- Latency sensitivity: summarization can tolerate ~400–600ms token latency; chat needs <250ms for tail.

Pricing / budget flags you mentioned
- You said procurement is targeting a long-term blended unit of roughly $600–$900 per 1M tokens (blended across workloads) depending on contract length and SLA.
- Early pilot budget: up to $120k/mo for initial 3 months to validate quality and cost curves.

Requested next steps from our side (can you confirm):
1) You confirm the volume ranges above and call out any additional workload flavors we missed.
2) Give us an internal procurement target (firm budget band / mandate) we should model to create the simulation.
3) Any technical constraints (regional data residency, KMS requirements) that would materially change cost or capacity needs.

What we’ll deliver by Fri (attached + short deck):
- A price simulation (spreadsheet) showing candidate $/1M token points and expected monthly invoice for pilot vs steady-state.
- A short benchmarking note comparing Redwood pricing to common hosts (OpenAI, Anthropic, three representative open-hosts) with performance caveats.
- A recommended target band and an implementation plan for the 3-month pilot (including toggles for quantization/batching to hit target economics).

Attached: Brightleaf_estimate_v1.xlsx (pilot vs steady-state simulation). Also uploading the call recording: call_recording_20270907.mp3.

If that captures it, I’ll loop Ben and Kim into the pricing detail thread and sketch a proposal for procurement.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks Jordan — that matches our conversation. Quick clarifications: 

- Volumes: you can model conservative / base / aggressive as 220M / 300M / 420M tokens/mo for summarization; chat add-on 40 / 50 / 80M tokens accordingly.
- Procurement target: leadership wants a long-term range of $550–$800 per 1M tokens, but procurement has formally greenlit $700–$950 for the pilot to move fast.
- Constraints: must host in us-east (data residency), and KMS required (we’ll share key policy). SOC 2 evidence already provided last week to your security contact.

Elena (cc procurement)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Sep 2027 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: BrightLeaf price simulation & target benchmarking — ask on target $/1M and comps

Ben / Kim — forwarding Elena’s confirmation. A few asks before I build the Exec-facing simulation: 

1) Benchmarks: quick sanity check on suggested target points and our positioning versus market. Elena called out leadership target $550–$800 and procurement pilot flexibility $700–$950. I’d like to propose an initial Redwood target band of $650–$800 per 1M (pilot discount structure to start at $750, ramp to $650 at commit). Thoughts?

2) Comparative comps (rough numbers for the note): please give me one-line bullets we can include in external doc:
   - OpenAI (gpt family) — typical list for heavy LLM gen at the point (approx): $900–1200 / 1M
   - Anthropic — approx: $700–950 / 1M (depends on model series)
   - Representative open-host A — 520–720 / 1M (lower cost but less predictable latency)
   - Representative open-host B — 480–680 / 1M (no SLA; requires customer-managed quant/ops)

3) Implementation levers to hit $650: quantized variant + aggressive batching for summarization, prefix caching on repeated docs, and scheduling background summarization during off-peak for large batches. Include the operational footnotes so procurement understands risk tradeoffs.

I’ve attached the first pass spreadsheet. I’ll produce a two-slide summary for procurement & leadership tomorrow morning.

— Jordan

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 08 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: BrightLeaf price simulation & target benchmarking — ask on target $/1M and comps

Jordan / Kim — quick notes from pricing side:

- The proposed Redwood band $650–$800 is defensible. For the pilot we should offer a two-tier: pilot effective $750/1M (30-day credit back if SLA misses >1% in month 1), scale commit to $650/1M at 6-12 month NRR-linked commit.
- Comps: I’d tighten the language on open-hosts: call them "community-hosted" or "self-managed hosts" and caveat that latency/ops burden varies wildly. The numbers you listed are fine as week-of-market approximations.
- Ask: include an explicit fallback model in the proposal — e.g., if latency is missed for chat paths we can route to a higher-price low-latency instance (preserve SLOs but increase cost). Put that in the slide.

I’ll review the spreadsheet and push a clean copy to the Drive link.

Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Commercial Pricing, Redwood Inference
